source.title: How polysemantic can one neuron be? Investigating features in TinyStories.

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE decoder-direction alignment to neurons, rather than measuring neuron responses to input examples, to examine how many features are associated with a neuron. This bears on feature packing but does not test the proposed capacity-pressure cause.
record.gate_note: The study reports feature-to-neuron alignment results, including a count for neuron 703. Its SAE reconstruction-loss and MLP-ablation-loss comparison is context about reconstruction, not a result on polysemanticity, so it is not a row. It does not directly measure neuron responses to unrelated inputs.
record.test_reason: The study uses a pre-trained SAE, which presupposes superposition, and counts how many SAE decoder directions have each MLP neuron as their largest component. It never measures neuron responses to unrelated inputs, how common polysemantic neurons are, or what causes them. Decoder-direction alignment is a related but different construct, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author finds neuron 703 is the most-aligned neuron for 475 SAE features, with sparse and non-sparse features roughly evenly split. The easiest-to-label (top-activation) features were spread across many neurons, not mostly on neuron 703. Features weighted toward neuron 703 were qualitatively harder to interpret. The post is exploratory and ends with open questions.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes SAE decoder directions and their alignment with MLP neuron dimensions, rather than examining neuron activations on input examples as in the cited vision example.

fits_no_version.finding: Neuron 703 is the top-aligned neuron for 475 SAE decoder directions. Some neurons are top-aligned for hundreds of features; most for only a handful.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In SAE decompositions of LM MLPs, feature decoder directions concentrate unevenly on a few neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: Qualitatively, features with more power on neuron 703 were harder to interpret than the high-activation features, which were spread across many neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Features more aligned with a heavily shared neuron are less interpretable.

record.problems: The analysis concerns one small pretrained model and the second/last layer, and the reported count is an alignment measure rather than a direct test of neuron responses to unrelated inputs. Feature interpretation is qualitative and limited to selected features; no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The text also describes qualitative comparisons between sparse and non-sparse feature directions and between selected feature groups, but does not report these as direct tests of the capacity-pressure mechanism or as measurements of neuron responses to unrelated inputs.

untested.parts: No share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts; no layer comparison.
No test that features outnumber neurons for capacity reasons, or that superposition causes polysemanticity; the SAE decomposition assumes it.
No initialization, regularization or training-noise manipulation.
No architecture, activation-function or regularization comparison.
Neuron 703's features are labelled qualitatively, but there is no test of whether they share one feature.
Activation range and explanation scoring are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: Informal LessWrong exploratory post on one small model, with no controls and no uncertainty estimates. The reader's V3 'supports' label is removed: decoder alignment presupposes superposition rather than testing it as the cause.

versions.untested_parts: No InceptionV1 neuron or vision-model responses are examined.
The study uses a language model but does not measure how often MLP neurons respond to unrelated tokens or contexts, or compare layers.

It measures SAE feature-direction alignment with neurons, but does not test whether feature count exceeds neuron count, whether capacity pressure causes the alignment, or whether the features are sparse in the sense required by the proposed mechanism.
No initialization, regularization, or training-noise mechanism is tested.
No activation-function, architecture, or regularization comparison, or performance-cost comparison, is conducted.
The study does not test whether canonical neurons' mixed inputs share a feature or job.
The study does not systematically vary activation range or explanation scoring.

rows.subject: TinyStories-2Layers-33M
rows.operation_detail: Counted, for each SAE feature, the neuron with the greatest power in its decoder direction.

conditions.value: 32,768 features; findings are not assigned to a specific one of the two SAEs examined

rows.measure: Number of SAE feature directions for which each neuron was the most-aligned neuron
rows.value: Neuron 703 was the most-aligned neuron for 475 features.
rows.note: This measures feature-direction alignment with a neuron; it does not establish that the neuron itself responds to 475 unrelated inputs or that capacity pressure caused the alignment.
rows.check: Counts SAE decoder directions whose largest component is neuron 703 (475 of 32,768). It does not show the neuron fires on unrelated inputs or test whether capacity pressure causes the packing. The V3 link and the 'observed' state are unsupported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported SAE feature directions in the layer-1 TinyStories MLP
reader_labels.reason: The feature-to-neuron alignment count shows many feature directions sharing one neuron's direction; this supports feature packing in the measured sense, but not the proposed capacity-pressure cause (R1).
